If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in the 16–30 day horizon to correct for sentiment reversal lag.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (21–30 days) to capture momentum carryover.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to avoid overcorrection from prior negative sentiment.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and forecast deviates >1.5% from true path, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction in the opposite direction for the next 5-day window to align with sentiment drift.
